Irrawaddy River: a river splits the teams and is crossed only at a few fords. Teams start on opposite banks. The river has three fords (four with six or more players), and they are the chokepoints of the map. Elephants roam the bamboo forests, silver is plentiful, and Sufi and Udasi villages stand on both banks.

Hawai'i: a volcanic island crossed by lava flows that burn units that stay on them. Everyone shares the Big Island. Lava flows cut across it: units can cross them but are burned if they stop, so the ground between the flows decides where armies meet. Heiau temples stand on the island; capture them for native Hawaiian units. The sea is rich in fish and whales.

Atacama: a dry high desert whose salt flats hold the richest mines. There are no natives and few trees, and guanacos are the only hunt. Two trade routes cross the map, and most salt mines lie in the middle, on the salt flats where nothing can be built, so the centre is fought over all game.

Rockies: two mountain ranges face each other across a rich central valley. Each team holds one range, and only a few passes lead down. Forests and treasures are richest in the valley, and a trade route runs along one side of the map. One native nation, Cheyenne or Comanche, lives up in the mountains.

Alps: creeks, valleys and forests cut the land into narrow passages. There is no trade route and no natives: you fight on your own. Deer, chamois, elk and hares are plentiful, and silver and gold mines lie between the valleys. Watch every crossing: the creeks let an enemy come in behind your lines.
